warnings.loanRejection: 69% of loan applications get rejected. Don't waste 3 months finding out you can't borrow.
warnings.loanRejectionBody: The heartbreaking pattern: Malaysians find their dream home, negotiate the price, pay booking fees... then get loan rejection. Banks use the 70% DSR rule. If your debts exceed 70% of income, you're automatically rejected.
warnings.loanRejectionCTA: Use this calculator BEFORE you house hunt. Know your EXACT borrowing limit. Don't fall in love with a RM800,000 property when you can only borrow RM450,000. Calculate your eligibility in 60 seconds.

content.loanEligibilityUnderstanding: Understanding Loan Eligibility and DSR in Malaysia
content.loanEligibilityPara1: The Debt Service Ratio (DSR) is the primary metric Malaysian banks use to assess your ability to service additional debt. It represents the percentage of your gross monthly income used to pay all debt obligations. Bank Negara Malaysia guidelines typically limit DSR to a maximum of 70%, though some banks may be more conservative. A DSR calculation considers all your existing loans including home loans, car loans, personal loans, and credit card balances.
content.loanEligibilityPara2: Understanding your DSR is crucial before applying for any loan. If your DSR is already at 70%, you will not qualify for additional financing regardless of your income level. This is why financial planning and debt management are essential. Many people are surprised to learn they cannot borrow as much as they expected because existing commitments have already consumed their borrowing capacity.
content.loanEligibilityPara3: When calculating DSR, banks look at gross income (before deductions like EPF, SOCSO, and taxes) but consider your net obligations. If you have variable income from commissions or bonuses, banks typically average these over 6-12 months. For self-employed individuals, banks review tax returns and financial statements from the past 2-3 years to determine sustainable income levels.
content.loanEligibilityPara4: The maximum loan amount is calculated using the present value of an annuity formula, considering your available monthly payment capacity, interest rate, and loan tenure. A longer tenure allows you to borrow more with the same monthly payment, but you'll pay significantly more interest over time. For example, at 4.5% interest, extending from 20 to 30 years might increase borrowing capacity by 25% but nearly doubles total interest paid.
content.loanEligibilityPara5: Beyond DSR, banks consider other factors: credit score (CCRIS and CTOS reports), employment stability, age (loans must typically be repaid by age 65-70), loan-to-value ratio (LTV), and the type of property or asset being financed. Even with good DSR, poor credit history or unstable employment can result in loan rejection or higher interest rates. Maintaining good financial health across all these dimensions maximizes your borrowing power and secures favorable terms.

loanEligibility.q1: What is DSR and how does it affect loan eligibility?
loanEligibility.a1: Debt Service Ratio (DSR) is the percentage of your monthly income used to service debt obligations. Malaysian banks typically require DSR to be below 70%. A lower DSR indicates better financial health and increases your chances of loan approval with favorable terms.
loanEligibility.q2: What counts as existing commitments for DSR calculation?
loanEligibility.a2: Existing commitments include all monthly debt obligations such as home loans, car loans, personal loans, credit card installments, and education loans. Even if you're a guarantor for someone else's loan, banks may include a portion of that loan in your DSR calculation.
loanEligibility.q3: How can I improve my loan eligibility?
loanEligibility.a3: To improve eligibility, increase your income through salary raises or additional income sources, reduce existing debts by paying off smaller loans first, maintain a good credit score by paying bills on time, and consider a longer loan tenure to reduce monthly payments (though this increases total interest).
loanEligibility.q4: Can I borrow more if I have a higher income?
loanEligibility.a4: Yes, higher income generally allows higher loan amounts as long as your DSR remains within limits. However, banks also consider other factors like employment stability, credit history, age, and the loan-to-value ratio. A high income alone doesn't guarantee maximum loan approval.
loanEligibility.q5: What if my DSR is above 70%?
loanEligibility.a5: If your DSR exceeds 70%, most banks will not approve additional loans. Options include paying down existing debts to reduce commitments, finding a co-borrower to increase combined income, increasing your down payment to reduce loan amount needed, or waiting to improve your financial situation before applying.
